note: serial defines an atomic auto-increment field type 'serial' (SerialItem) with a hidden widget serial_default_widget and formatter serial_default_formatter. Storage settings: start_value (default 1) and init_existing_entities (0/1), schema field.storage_settings.serial. Value allocated in preSave() via the serial.sql_storage service using a per-field AUTO_INCREMENT assistant table serial_<md5(entityType_bundle_field)>; creating/deleting a serial FieldConfig auto-creates/drops that table (serial_field_config_create/delete). No admin page, permissions, Drush, or plugin types (configure=null). Medium cases create serial fields (field_srl_*) with known settings and the agent reads field.storage config back; hard cases create serial fields (start_value / with display formatter) verified against live field + display config. Only this module's own field_srl_* storages are ever created/deleted by name (never a broad field purge).

evals.prompt: I need each new node of a content type to get an automatic sequential number (like an invoice number) in Drupal. Which contrib module/field type gives me that, and how do editors enter the value?
evals.expected_output: Use the Serial module's 'serial' field type: add a Serial field to the bundle. Editors do NOT enter it — the widget is 'Hidden (Automatic)' (serial_default_widget) and the next number is assigned automatically on save.

evals.prompt: What options can I configure when creating a Serial field in Drupal, e.g. the number it starts at and back-filling existing content? Name the storage settings.
evals.expected_output: Two storage settings set at field-creation time: start_value (default 1, the first number) and init_existing_entities (No/Yes — whether to assign serial values to entities that already exist in the bundle). Both are locked once the field has data.

evals.prompt: How does the Drupal Serial module guarantee unique, atomic sequential numbers even under concurrent entity creation? What does it create per field?
evals.expected_output: For each serial field it creates a dedicated 'assistant' table named serial_<md5(entityType_bundle_field)> with a real database AUTO_INCREMENT (sid) column. To allocate a number the serial.sql_storage service inserts a temporary row inside a transaction and returns the DB-generated sid, so allocation is atomic and race-free.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the Article content type has a Serial field named field_srl_known. Inspect the live field storage configuration and tell me the starting value it was configured with.
evals.expected_output: The starting value is 1000 — field.storage.node.field_srl_known settings.start_value = 1000.

evals.prompt: The Article content type on this site has several fields. Inspect the live field configuration and tell me the machine name of the field that is a Serial (auto-increment) field.
evals.expected_output: field_srl_auto is the serial field (field.storage.node.field_srl_auto type = serial); field_srl_plain is a plain integer, not serial.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use the Serial module to add an auto-increment field with machine name field_srl_task to the Article content type, configured to start numbering at 500. Apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: field.storage.node.field_srl_task exists with type 'serial' and settings.start_value = 500, and the field is attached to the article bundle.

evals.prompt: On this site add a Serial field named field_srl_evt to the Article content type, and make the number visible on the article's default display using the Serial default formatter. Apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: field.storage.node.field_srl_evt is type 'serial' and core.entity_view_display.node.article.default shows field_srl_evt with formatter type serial_default_formatter.
